concepts.def: Softens on heating; weak intermolecular forces

walkthroughs.body_html:
Thermosoftening polymers have weak forces between chains and can be remelted.

Thermosetting polymers have covalent cross-links - rigid and cannot be remelted.

Fermentation: glucose + yeast -> ethanol + CO2.

Or hydration: ethene + steam -> ethanol with phosphoric acid catalyst.

Acid + alcohol with H2SO4 catalyst -> ester + water.

Used as flavourings and perfumes.

mcqs.q: Thermosetting polymers cannot be remelted because:
When water boils, what is broken?
options: The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
A primary alcohol is oxidised to an alkene by losing water.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.
A primary alcohol is oxidised to an alkene by losing water.
Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.

mcqs.q: What is the product of mild oxidation of a primary alcohol?
options: A primary alcohol is oxidised directly to a ketone.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
An aldehyde (which can be further oxidised to a carboxylic acid).
A primary alcohol is oxidised to an alkene by losing water.
